items.title: Firing squad execution to be livestreamed, Pentagon says
items.description: Pete Hegseth says the execution will be public, but a legal expert says the "unprecedented" decision is on "uncertain legal terrain".

items.title: Fort Hood survivor supports gunman's execution by firing squad but questions livestream
items.description: Alonzo Lunsford tells the BBC the punishment befits the crime but he has some doubts whether the public should be able to watch it.

items.title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire speaks to BBC
items.description: Vitalii Zhykovych gives his own account of the attempted assassination of Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev.

items.title: Thieves steal 30,000 wine bottles worth €5m in Italy, reports say
items.description: The heist at the Florence-based winery is believed to be one of the largest thefts of its kind in Italy.

items.title: ICE agent shoots man in New York City
items.description: The mayor of New York expressed outrage at the shooting which the Department of Homeland Security said happened during the arrest of a "criminal illegal alien".

items.title: Three Saudi nationals killed in Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport
items.description: The missile attacks come amid an escalation in fighting between the Iran-backed group and Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's government.

items.title: Russian strikes and approaching winter force some in Kyiv to pack bags and flee
items.description: A renewed Russian campaign of strikes on power and energy infrastructure has made some contemplate leaving Ukraine's capital.

items.title: Christa Pike has 'profound' health turnaround after botched execution, lawyers say
items.description: Pike's lawyers say her recovery is "remarkable" as they give an update on her condition after she survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.

items.title: Fired OpenAI researchers say they were let go for 'prioritising safety'
items.description: The AI firm instead claims the researchers were fired for mishandling sensitive information.

items.title: Cars torched and shops looted as anti-migrant violence erupts in South Africa
items.description: South Africa has experienced recurrent outbreaks of violence, often targeting migrants from neighbouring countries.

items.title: Adidas sues Australian label White Fox over four stripes design
items.description: The German sportswear brand wants the Sydney-based label to stop selling the clothes and pay damages.

items.title: 'Bold and inventive' Canadian poet Anne Carson wins Nobel Literature Prize
items.description: Carson, 76, is celebrated for works that often cross boundaries between poetry, fiction and scholarship.

items.title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture
items.description: The new accusations relate to the alleged torture of US citizens held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.

items.title: Teacher who sexually abused pupil back in Indonesia jail after BBC investigation
items.description: Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani had been secretly released on parole in 2025, after serving less than half his sentence.

items.title: Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam'
items.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni says the move will deliver more stable government, but opposition parties say her aim is to stay in power.

items.title: US deportations to African countries unlawful and exploit suffering, rights group says
items.description: More than 500 migrants have been expelled from the US to African countries, HRW says, citing US data.

items.title: Outspoken Indian actor Nana Patekar dies suddenly at 75
items.description: Known for his intense performances, Patekar carved out a distinctive place in Indian cinema.

items.title: Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile
items.description: The Mapocho river has burst its banks after an unusually large amount of rain fell in recent days.

items.title: Zambia signs US health deal after disputes over data-sharing
items.description: The US will provide $1.5bn (£1.1bn) under the deal that was negotiated after Trump cut USAID funding.

items.title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says
items.description: Casualties have been reported on the vessel, identified by a maritime intelligence firm as the oil and chemical tanker, Acers.
